changes, create PR\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd style=\"height: 54.3892px;\"\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003eView diffs in sidebar, stage commits, open PR without leaving Cursor\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003eThe shift is not fro\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003em hard to easy. It is from writing to directing. You spend less time on implementation and more time defining requirements and reviewing output. Whether that trade is worth it depends on the task, and honestly on how much you trust the agent on a given day.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eLong-running tasks benefit most. A refactor that would take hours in a terminal can go to a cloud agent, you close your laptop, the agent keeps going, and the diffs are waiting when you get back.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eCursor 3 vs. Previous Versions of Cursor\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eEarly Cursor (2022 to 2024) was an IDE-first tool. AI-assisted file editing in a VS Code environment.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eCursor 1.0 (June 2025) was the first stable release. Cursor 2.0 (October 2025) brought the first Composer model and in-app browser. Cursor 2.5 (February 2026) added async subagents and the plugin marketplace. Cursor 2.6 (March 2026) added team marketplaces.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eCursor 3.0 makes the shift official. Cloud agents moved out of the Editor entirely and now live exclusively in the Agents Window. Worktree support also changed: the old dropdown UI was deprecated and replaced with the \u003ccode\u003e/worktree\u003c/code\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/best-of-n\u003c/code\u003e \u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003ecommands, which run in the classic editor chat. If you have internal documentation on how to use the worktree dropdown or start cloud agents from inside the Editor, it is outdated.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eCursor used the 3.0 rebuild to clear performance debt from 2.x: memory and CPU leak patches, the React Compiler. Robinson described the result as faster and less prone to UI jank. Windows is fully supported, and the interface handles multiple workspaces in a single window.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eThe jump from 2.x to 3.0 is more structural than it looks. Earlier versions added agent features to an IDE. Cursor 3 adds an IDE to an agent platform. That order matters.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eCursor 3 vs. Traditional IDEs\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eTraditional IDEs are file-centric. You open a file, edit text, and the IDE helps you type faster. Even with GitHub Copilot installed, the abstraction is still the document.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eCursor 3 makes the file secondary. The primary interface is the task queue. The IDE becomes the fallback for edits too specific to describe in a prompt.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eThe comparison is getting murkier though. GitHub Copilot now offers cloud agents and code review across individual plan tiers. JetBrains bundles Junie, its own autonomous coding agent, with AI subscriptions. And as mentioned earlier, Cursor now runs inside JetBrains IDEs via ACP. Everyone has agents now. The real difference with Cursor 3 is that the workspace was built around them rather than added to an existing editor.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eLimitations and Open Questions\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eThe day-to-day experience has more friction than the launch materials suggest.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eDeveloper oversight\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eAgents make errors. On complex multi-file tasks, they make a lot of them. Reviewing agent output requires enough familiarity with the codebase to catch incorrect assumptions, hallucinated functions, and logic that almost works. The time saved on writing shifts to reading and validating. Developers who cannot read the generated code to check it will not be able to keep the codebase working. That is not a knock on Cursor specifically; it applies to every agentic coding tool.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eCloud agent reliability\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eEnvironment setup failures are a documented and ongoing issue. Secrets cannot be injected during the initial setup script, only post-setup. Extended parallel sessions consume significant resources; users have reported heavy RAM usage on machines that should handle it. Keep sessions under two hours if you can, and add re-indexing checkpoints for anything longer.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eOne more specific gap: Plan Mode is not yet available in the Cursor web UI. You can start and run cloud agents including planning from the Cursor 3 desktop app, but not from \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca style=\"text-decoration: none;\" href=\"https://cursor.com/agents\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: underline; -webkit-text-decoration-skip: none; text-decoration-skip-ink: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003ecursor.com/agents\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003e directly.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eThere is also a known bug where agents hang when the Agents Window is not in focus. It was reported shortly after launch and was unresolved as of early April 2026. For a tool built around long-running sessions, that is a real problem.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eOn parallel agents more broadly: Google DeepMind research on multi-agent systems found error amplification of up to 17.2 times in unstructured networks. Even at 99% per-agent reliability, ten chained agents drop to about 90% overall. The \u003c/span\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/best-of-n\u003c/code\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003e command uses isolated worktrees, which limits some of this. It does not eliminate it.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eSecurity considerations\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eTwo CVEs were found and patched in 2025. CVE-2025-54136 (MCPoison) allowed approved MCP tools to have their commands silently modified; patched in version 1.3. CVE-2025-64106 was a deep-link remote code execution vulnerability with a severity score of 8.8, patched within two days. Workspace Trust is also disabled by default. If you are connecting MCP tools in a sensitive environment, that matters.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eSelf-hosted cloud agents, as I covered earlier, keep agent work inside your network, but the Cursor platform itself is not available as a full on-premises deployment. Cursor does not hold FedRAMP or HIPAA certification. BAA availability is not publicly documented, so confirm directly with Cursor before relying on it for compliance decisions. If your environment requires FedRAMP or full on-premises deployment, Cursor 3 is not a fit.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eTwo more practical limitations worth flagging: Design Mode currently works only in Chrome; Firefox and Safari are not supported. And in the days following the Cursor 3 launch, community reports documented Composer 2 token consumption running roughly 10 times higher than normal for some users, linked to cache read issues.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch3 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eThe credit model\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eAs I covered in the parallel agents section, each \u003c/span\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/best-of-n\u003c/code\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003e model charges separately. A three-model comparison on a complex task can drain a large portion of your monthly pool in a single session.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eWho Should Use Cursor 3?\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eIf you are already running agent-assisted workflows and want everything in one place, this is built for you. It makes the most sense for teams working across multiple repos, for longer tasks you can hand off to the cloud, and for enterprise teams that need code to stay inside their own infrastructure.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eI would not recommend it for beginners. Not because it is hard to use, but because agents produce code you have to read critically. If you cannot tell when the output is wrong, you cannot fix it, and six months later the codebase will show that. For simple scripts or one-off tasks, the setup overhead is not worth it either. And if your environment is HIPAA-regulated or air-gapped, see the Security section before going further.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eLarge legacy monorepos are also a real problem. Context windows still break on them.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eThe Future of AI Coding with Cursor\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eIn February 2026, \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca style=\"text-decoration: none;\" href=\"https://cursor.com/blog/self-driving-codebases\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: underline; -webkit-text-decoration-skip: none; text-decoration-skip-ink: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eCursor published\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003e \"Towards Self-Driving Codebases,\" describing experiments with thousands of orchestrated agents across large codebases. The stated goal: \"until codebases are self-driving.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eContext windows still break on large monorepos. Agents hallucinate regularly. The vision is far enough out that I would not plan around it.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eWhat Cursor 3 does is put the main pieces in place: a model in Composer 2, an interface in the Agents Window, cloud VMs as the runtime, and self-hosted options for enterprise. The self-driving codebase depends on model improvements Cursor does not fully control.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eTruell's \"factory\" framing is still a long way from reality. For now, you are still the one reviewing the factory floor.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003ch2 dir=\"ltr\"\u003eConclusion\u003c/h2\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eCursor 3's main change is not a feature. It is that the interface was rebuilt around a different assumption: that the agent, not the file, is the unit of work. Two years ago that was a bet. The usage data suggests it is paying off.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan style=\"background-color: transparent; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-decoration: none; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;\"\u003eWhether it fits your workflow depends on things I cannot determine from here: codebase size, security requirements, and whether you can live with a product that launched weeks ago and still has rough edges.
